stem: An infant develops rhinorrhea and decreased feeding followed by cough, wheezing, and increased work of breathing. Which viral infection is most consistent with this pattern?
rationale: CDC describes RSV in infants and young children as often beginning with runny nose and decreased appetite, followed by cough; wheezing and difficulty breathing can develop as the illness progresses. The other choices have different characteristic clinical patterns.
educational_objective: Recognize the typical progression of RSV illness in an infant.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source_document_title: RSV in Infants and Young Children; Symptoms and Care of RSV
source_locator: Early symptoms and progression—runny nose/decreased appetite followed by cough, wheezing, and difficulty breathing
source_claim_supported: RSV in infants commonly progresses from upper-respiratory symptoms to cough, wheezing, and breathing difficulty.
correction_summary: Removed the unsupported assumption that the findings alone establish bronchiolitis and tested the CDC-described RSV pattern.
audit_findings: The symptom progression closely matches CDC RSV guidance.
Other viral choices have characteristic findings absent from the stem.
Independent second pass found one best answer.
